glosses: to discern, to distinguish, to discriminate
to become different
различать, отличать
być świadomym różnic, dostrzegać różnice
To recognize someone or something as different from others based on its characteristics.

examples.text: It had begun to take a leading place even in the days of the Ptolemies, and in scientific, as distinguished from purely literary work, it had assumed a position of primary importance early in the Christian era.
The physics of elementary particles in the 20th century was distinguished by the observation of particles whose existence had been predicted by theorists sometimes decades earlier.

glosses: To see someone or something clearly or distinctly.
To make noticeably different or better from others through accomplishments.

examples.text: The soldier distinguished himself in combat and received a medal.

1784: William Jones, The Description and Use of a New Portable Orrery, &c., PREFACE
THE favourable reception the Orrery has met with from Perſons of the firſt diſtinction, and from Gentlemen and Ladies in general, has induced me to add to it ſeveral new improvements in order to give it a degree of Perfection; and diſtinguiſh it from others; which by Piracy, or Imitation, may be introduced to the Public.

glosses: To confer an honor upon.

examples.text: The soldier was distinguished with a medal for his bravery.

glosses: To make to differ.
To detect with the senses, especially with the eyes.

examples.text: Meanwhile the brig had altered her tack, and was moving slowly to the east. Three hours later and the keenest eye could not have discerned her top-sails above the horizon.

glosses: To perceive, recognize, or comprehend with the mind; to descry.

examples.text: If they discern any evidences of wrong-going in any direction that I have indicated, they will acknowledge that I had reason in what I wrote. If they discern no such thing, they will consider me altogether mistaken.

glosses: To distinguish something as being different from something else; to differentiate or discriminate.

examples.text: He was too young to discern right from wrong.

The severity of judgement, they say, makes men censorious and unapt to pardon the errors and infirmities of other men: and on the other side, celerity of fancy makes the thoughts less steady than is necessary to discern exactly between right and wrong.

Poder ver o comprender la diferencia entre dos cosas.
Hacer que una cosa sea diferente de otras.
Otorgar una cualidad o característica individual.
Demostrar especial estima hacia una persona.
Otorgar un honor o dignidad a una persona.
Hacer distinción, conocer la diversidad de las cosas; dar a cada una su correspondiente y legítimo valor.
Variar, mudar el uso que se hace de las cosas.
Hallar la diferencial de una cantidad variable.
Discordar, no convenir en un mismo parecer u opinión.
oder mit zwischen: einen Unterschied machen; feststellen, dass etwas verschieden ist

examples.text: Es wird in der englischen Grammatik nicht zwischen verschiedenen Genera unterschieden.
Martin kann leider Spiel und Ernst nicht unterscheiden.
Der Großvater konnte die Zwillinge noch nie unterscheiden.

glosses: anders sein als etwas oder jemand, mit dem verglichen wird

examples.text: Sie unterscheiden sich von uns in dem Punkt, dass sie sich nie waschen.

„In einer Zeit, da ein Mittelklassewagen wie der andere aussieht und sich auch moderne Verkehrsflugzeuge im Design nur unwesentlich voneinander unterscheiden, ist der Airbus A 380 eben ein besonderes Fluggerät.“
Dein Bleistift und meiner unterscheiden sich doch vom Äußeren her kaum.

glosses: optische oder akustische Sinneswahrnehmungen jemandem oder etwas zuordnen

examples.text: In dem Nebel kann ich die Personen nicht mehr unterscheiden.
Konnten Sie die Stimme der Angeklagten deutlich unterscheiden?
